content:
If you're willing to wait a little while rather than rushing to buy Apple's new products on day one, Apple's official refurbished store has always been a good option. Generally speaking, you have to wait about three months after a new product launches before the refurbished model first appears on Apple's website.

Other companies offer similar options, such as Amazon Renewed and Walmart Restored, but be aware that they use different quality standards and warranty terms...

Apple Certified Refurbished

Buying from Apple's Certified Refurbished store typically gets you about a 15% discount, and the product itself is almost identical to a brand-new one. Specifically, Apple guarantees all of the following:

  • Full inspection and testing by Apple
  • Brand-new housing with no marks or scratches whatsoever
  • Brand-new battery with the same battery life as a new product
  • Includes all original accessories and cables
  • Comes with the same Apple standard one-year warranty as a new product
  • Also eligible for purchasing AppleCare+

Basically the only difference you'll see is that the product comes in a plain white box rather than the original packaging.

Amazon Renewed

Amazon Renewed's pricing may be more competitive, but note that you won't get the same quality assurance:

  • Inspection and testing is done by the seller, not Apple
  • The housing is second-hand and expected to have marks and scratches (see below)
  • The battery is second-hand and only guaranteed to have at least 80% of original capacity
  • Accessories may not be genuine Apple products
  • Comes with a 90-day Amazon warranty, not Apple's one-year warranty

Regarding marks and scratches, Amazon offers three quality tiers:

  • Premium/Excellent: No visible signs of cosmetic damage when viewed from 12 inches away
  • Good: Has minor scratches that are barely noticeable when holding the device from 12 inches away
  • Acceptable: Has clearly visible and tactile scratches

Walmart Restored

Walmart Restored is much vaguer than Amazon about what you're getting:

  • Makes no promises about cosmetic condition, only claiming "like-new performance and reliability"
  • Provides no specific information about battery condition beyond the above description
  • Offers no information about accessories
  • Warranty is provided by the seller, not Apple's one-year warranty

The Restored Premium tier comes with a one-year seller warranty, while Like New, Good, and Fair tiers only get 90 days. The company doesn't clearly define what each tier means.

9to5Mac's Take

If you want something that's identical to a new product both cosmetically and in terms of Apple's warranty, then Apple's refurbished store is clearly the top choice.

However, Amazon Renewed's pricing can indeed be a lot cheaper, and if you're willing to accept the trade-offs mentioned above, you might find it a decent option. Especially if you're planning to follow our advice and save money by upgrading to the iPhone 17 Pro instead of this year's latest model (since you just won't get a cable), there are several attractive deals here:

  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Cosmic Orange $1,214 (original $1,499) — All-time low price
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Deep Blue $1,215 (original $1,499) — All-time low price
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Silver $1,208 (original $1,499) — All-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Cosmic Orange $1,164 (original $1,299) — All-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Deep Blue $1,170 (original $1,299) — All-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Silver $1,171 (original $1,299) — Just $1 off the all-time low price

As for Walmart Restored, I'd have reservations because their promises are too vague, but if you're not satisfied, you can indeed choose to return it.
